document_0002.source_limits: King & Saraf re-test the central claim of Ioannou & Serafeim (2015), I&S: that over 1993-2007 sell-side analysts' recommendations became less pessimistic for firms with high CSR (KLD) strengths. They state that they 'analyze the same data, use the same statistical models, and recreate the main tables', rebuilding the original sample from the same databases (Compustat, CRSP, I/B/E/S, KLD; N=16,088 vs 16,064 originally). I therefore code a reproduction (re-analysis of the original study's data) rather than a new-sample replication. Part of the extension adds new years through 2016; that new-data portion is not used for the robustness axis. Single original paper, one target; the replication paper reports no numbered studies. Axis 1 (computation): the re-run produced numbers, but they did not recover the original pattern. The authors write 'Unlike I&S', report no substantive or significant change in the CSR coefficient over time, and say Tables 3-4 provide no support for the principal hypothesis. They also report coefficient differences for market value and long-term forecast error, and the replicated auxiliary/robustness analyses differ from I&S. This is coded 'computational issues'. Descriptive statistics broadly conform. The divergence may partly reflect reconstruction choices, such as lag structure and the forecast-error formula; the original authors did not respond. Axis 2 (robustness): alternative specifications of the original 1993-2007 frame removed the claimed temporal shift: CSR x linear time, CSR x year dummies, and analyst-level models with analyst fixed effects. The authors conclude that the finding 'is not as robust as previously suggested'. This is coded 'robustness challenges'. A qualifier is that the analyst-level models show a positive linear trend for CSR concerns, significant only in the extended (new-data) sample, and a lone significant 1996 strengths estimate. Source limits: the supplied text is pdftotext output. Tables 3, 4 and 6 and Figures 1-3 appear only as captions, so the reproduced coefficients for the main tables cannot be inspected. I rely on the authors' prose. No DOI for I&S is printed in the reference list. Ioannou & Serafeim's reference entry is copied with line-wrap hyphenation removed in the title field.

document_0003.source_limits: Wismans et al. (2020), a 'Replication Note', re-test in a new sample a finding from Yu, Wiklund & Pérez-Luño (2018). The new sample comprises 802 French SME owners from three Amarok survey waves. Yu et al., using Spanish and mainly US samples, found that firm-level EO is positively related to the hyperactivity/impulsivity dimension of ADHD and unrelated to the attention-deficit dimension. This is a replication (new data, individual-level EO, different controls) with one target. The 2018 Academy of Management Proceedings version is named because the authors cite it throughout and state that they based the replication on it rather than the forthcoming 2020 ETP version. Its DOI is printed in the reference list. Outcome: there is no single overall verdict, but the discussion compares both of Yu et al.'s dimension-level results. Hyperactivity is positively associated with total EO ('Similar to Yu et al.'; 'we are able to replicate the positive relationship found by Yu et al. (2018) between hyperactivity and EO'). Attention-deficit is not associated with total EO, which agrees with Yu et al.'s null. The authors call their results 'mostly in line' with Yu et al., and no result is marked as contrasting with the original, so this is coded successful. The null total-ADHD-EO link and the EO subdimension results are extensions: the paper states that no prior study examined overall ADHD and EO and that Yu et al. did not split EO. They therefore do not count against the replication verdict. Qualifiers: the word 'mostly'; differing controls; low alpha for hyperactivity (.51); individual- rather than firm-level EO. Thurik et al. (2016, retracted) is not coded as a target. The paper says it 'redo[es] the analysis of Thurik et al. (2016)' on an overlapping sample, but with the stated aim of replicating Yu et al. It never states or compares against a Thurik et al. finding. Source limits: text is a cached parse of the published PDF. Tables 2 and 3 are rotated and extracted one character per line; their values were read only as scrambled characters, and the coding relies on the prose results and discussion. A machine-parsed reference list is appended after the article references.

document_0008.source_limits: Psychiatric Services (2011) author manuscript from PMC, full text including reference list read in four chunks. The paper is a new randomized trial (N=160 women, HMO members) designed to 'replicate and extend' the authors' own published earlier trial of CBT guided self-help for recurrent binge eating (ref 23, Striegel-Moore et al. 2010, J Consult Clin Psychol), with modified recruitment, a self-report EDE-Q instead of the EDE interview, and a narrower age range; new data on a new sample make it a replication of a published finding, not a within-paper self-replication. Table 2 places this study's effect sizes beside those of the 'Previous efficacy trial' sourced from ref 23. One target: ref 23. Ref 39 (Lynch et al. 2010, cost-effectiveness of the same earlier trial) is cited alongside 23 when describing the original study, but this paper reports no cost-effectiveness analysis to compare (only descriptive service-use data), so it is not re-tested and is excluded; ref 26 (recruitment report) is background. Single replicating study, so replication_study_numbers is empty. Source limits: HTML get_text flattening removed line structure and merged table cells into running text (Tables 1-3 are readable only as flattened sequences); no images or figures beyond tables are present in the supplied text, so no visual coverage is claimed. Placeholder underscores in the source table values (e.g. '_78__') are reproduced as in the source.
document_0008.field_specific_caution: Assigned correction is original identity; outcome agreement is not sufficient. Source internal effect-size contradiction remains relevant context.
document_0008.parent_scientific_comparison: Both fresh coders identify Ref23 clinical trial and successful outcome. document_0009.source_limits: Working paper (draft of December 12, 2015, 'Comments solicited'; UCR economics working-paper PDF via pdftotext) titled 'A Replication of Thomas Piketty's Data on the Distribution of Wealth for the United States'. Despite the word 'replication', the work re-analyses the original author's own published data, spreadsheets and documented sources rather than collecting new data, so under the codebook it is a reproduction. Single target: Piketty (2014a) Capital in the Twenty-First Century (the book whose U.S. top-1% and top-10% wealth-share series, Figures 10.5 and 10.6, are re-derived). Piketty (2014b) Technical Appendix and the TS10.1 spreadsheet are the original's documentation, not separate findings. Piketty and Saez (2014, Science) is excluded as a separate target: the paper reproduces its Figure 2 as Figure 4 but says it re-presents the book's Figure 10.6 data, and the assessment is framed against the book (borderline exclusion recorded in evidence_map.json). Data sources (Kopczuk and Saez 2004, Wolff, Kennickell, Soltow, Lindert, Saez and Zucman 2015) and earlier critiques (Giles 2014, Magness and Murphy 2015) are not targets. No DOI for the book is printed. Source limits: Figures 1-4 are charts not present in the supplied text (only surrounding captions/discussion), so no visual coverage is claimed; pdftotext layout interleaves footnotes and page numbers with body text; the text is a draft working paper, not a published version.
document_0009.field_specific_caution: Opus omits Piketty/Saez2014 as a separate target and is not confident about computation. Neither target omission nor label agreement authorizes a record removal or joint type/outcome correction.

document_0013.source_limits: Hafeez and Quintana-Domeque re-test, with new data from Pakistan (2006-07 PDHS, 6,955 children), the published findings of Jayachandran and Kuziemko (2011) on son preference and gender-biased breastfeeding in India, and the additional sex-composition-by-gender prediction of Chakravarty (2015) in Egypt. This is a replication (different sample, re-tested published findings) and is completed. Two targets: JK 2011 (predictions 1-3, 5-7, 9) and Chakravarty 2015 (prediction 4, which the authors attribute to Chakravarty and compare against directly). Chakravarty is not merely background: the paper re-tests his own added prediction and replicates his specification. Excluded: Kennedy et al. 1989 and Kazi et al. 1995 (medical background on lactational amenorrhea), Hussain et al. 2000 (supplied the unwantedness variable and is critiqued, not re-tested), Arnold 1997 (stated son-preference ratios used to interpret magnitudes), and the authors' own new prediction 8 (not a published finding). JK outcome mixed: the authors state support for all JK predictions except 9 and mark a contrast on the post-threshold trend. Chakravarty outcome successful: the authors state their result is consistent with Chakravarty. Source limits: the supplied text is a pdftotext -layout extraction. Figures 1-4 are images not present in the text; only their captions and the authors' prose descriptions were available, so no visual coverage is claimed. Online appendices A1 and A2 (sample restrictions, alternate explanations) are not included. Table cells and equations have extraction artifacts: minus signs render as "2" (e.g. "2.093" for -.093), "=" as "5" and "+" as "1"; table values were read with this in mind and are not used as the basis of any verdict. No DOI is printed for either target.
